Aircraft composite structures are prone to barely visible damages like delamination and matrix cracks requiring structural health monitoring.
Guided wave (GW) and piezoelectric sensor network–based damage imaging techniques offer large-scale monitoring and high localization accuracy.
Time-varying environmental conditions, especially temperature variations, introduce uncertainties in GW signals that mask damage effects.
The proposed method uses Gaussian mixture models (GMM) to model uncertainties in damage indexes extracted from GW signals.
Two damage indexes (DI1 and DI2) are used: time domain cross-correlation and spectrum magnitude difference.
The baseline GMM is constructed from healthy structure signals under varying conditions and updated continuously with monitoring signals.
Kullback–Leibler divergence is used to measure the difference between baseline and monitoring GMMs to characterize damage.
Damage imaging is performed by synthesizing probabilistic ellipses from all GW paths in the sensor network.
Accumulation imaging generates a series of images over time, allowing damage to gradually emerge for reliable localization.
Experimental validation was conducted on a stiffened carbon fiber composite plate with temperature variation from 0°C to 60°C.
The method achieved reliable damage imaging and localization within the tested temperature range.
The GMM-based approach suppresses time-varying influences and achieves time-varying-independent damage characterization.
Existing methods often rely on baseline signals and do not adequately handle time-varying environmental effects.
The proposed method does not require compensation for each environmental condition and works under complex structural geometries.
The sensor network used consists of multiple piezoelectric transducers (PZTs) forming multiple GW paths.
Damage indexes are extracted from signals without needing a fixed baseline, enhancing robustness under variable conditions.
The method combines statistical modeling with physical sensor network data fusion for damage localization.
The probabilistic ellipse's area correlates positively with damage severity.
The method iteratively updates the GMM parameters using expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm.
The approach is validated for practical aerospace structural health monitoring applications.
